# Images

Images were stressed as important on both days: one in six AI Mode searches is multimodal (Day 1), and on Day 2 Google said images and videos drive a large amount of publisher traffic and that an extracted image can appear in web search, Google Images, Discover and AI features. Google finds images through img elements in the HTML (a picture element counts only through the img inside it) and through image sitemaps, cannot index an image without a src, and does not extract CSS background images; to keep images out of results, its documentation names a robots.txt disallow or a noindex X-Robots-Tag header. Alt text should describe the image for someone who cannot see it and can make the image rank for what it names; Google's image guide calls alt the most important attribute for image metadata, while Gary Illyes ranked it below src and said Google uses only three img attributes (said at the event, not in Google's docs). Day 2 confirmed part of Day 1's slide of image signals (resolution, colour and associated text; the list itself is not in Google's docs): the surrounding text is critical context for understanding and ranking an image, which Google's image guide supports. Google supports nearly all popular formats and recommends modern ones such as WebP with small files; Gary Illyes said the AVIF format currently has ingestion hiccups (heard in two independent recordings), although Google's image guide lists AVIF as supported. Day 3 added Discover and Search Console: Google's Discover slides tie click-through to image quality and recommend images at least 1,200 px wide, over 300,000 pixels and 16x9, enabled by max-image-preview:large, with no logos or text-heavy images. Search Console's multimodal search type, rolling out from 24 September 2026, reports searches with Lens, Circle to Search, uploaded images and Chrome's image search, without a query dimension. Google said image results among web results come from its image index, that an image query is searched as embeddings, and that images are indexed in hours to two days on average while changing the image shown with a text result takes 1-2 weeks (said at the event, not in Google's docs). The second recordings added more. On Day 1 Google said the search box is multimodal, that Lens was its answer to young users uploading pictures and expecting answers about them, and that Lens is used by over 1.5 billion people (Google's May 2025 post says every month); for visual search Google breaks an image into vectors and returns results from the index based on them, and Gary Illyes said searching by image or video was not possible before transformers (both said at the event). On Day 2 he said the media indexer attaches each image and video to the URL of the page that hosts it, that Googlebot-Image rules or a disallowed file location keep images out, that noimageindex also stops videos because their thumbnails are images (not in Google's docs), and that max-image-preview:large can make content do surprisingly well in Discover. On AI-generated images Google said the choice is up to the site owner, that Google shows them when users look for them, and that diffusion models are poor at text inside images, so sites should check them for hallucinations and regenerate where needed; Google's image metadata guide supports IPTC digital source types and C2PA details for AI-made images. In Lightning session F a community speaker showed LLM-rewritten alt text going wrong: for a cat anxiety medicine the model described only a cat and a vet, dropping the page's intent, and the site's image performance in Search Console fell; the safer script adds the page title to the image description and is tested on a few URLs first. Author's view: visual search predates transformers in Google's own history (Google Images 2001, Lens 2017), so the remark is about today's multimodal AI search; and do not set noimageindex on video watch pages.

## What to do

- Put every image that should rank in an img element with a real src (inside picture if you serve several formats); keep CSS backgrounds for decorative images.
- Write alt text that describes the image for someone who cannot see it, and place a caption or explanatory sentence next to important images.
- Set max-image-preview:large on indexable templates unless licensing forbids it, and check that no CMS, plug-in or CDN default lowers it.
- Keep images out of Google with a robots.txt disallow for Googlebot-Image or a noindex X-Robots-Tag header, not with CSS backgrounds.
- If you serve AVIF, keep a WebP or JPEG file in the img src and offer AVIF through source elements inside picture while the ingestion hiccup Gary Illyes mentioned lasts, then check in Google Images that key images appear.
- Use original images with descriptive file names, and list images Google may not find in an image sitemap.
- Track image-led traffic with Search Console's multimodal search type, by page, country and device.
- Review AI-written alt text before a rollout: test it on a few URLs, and give the model the page's title or intent so the text carries more than what the image shows.
- Check AI-generated images for garbled text and other hallucinations, and regenerate them where needed.

- **[Stage]** The diffusion models that generate images were built to generate images, not text, so they are typically poor at rendering text inside an image.
  <br><sub>`D2-C939` · Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos (Gary Illyes) · not in Google docs · Extended by [D3-C688](../../40-sessions/day3/D3-S18-wrapping-all-up-ai-search-and-making-sense-of-everything.md) · Used by `DEV-IMG-08`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Gary Illyes showed a timeline image that Google made with an image generation model in 2025 and deliberately left unfixed as a counterexample: its text was garbled and its years jumped from 1994 to 1995 and back to 1994.
  <br><sub>`D2-C940` · Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos (Gary Illyes)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Sites that use AI-generated images or videos should make sure they work for users, check them for hallucinations and regenerate them where needed.
  <br><sub>`D2-C941` · Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [Google Search's guidance on using generative AI content on your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/using-gen-ai-content) · Extended by [D3-C700](../../40-sessions/day3/D3-S18-wrapping-all-up-ai-search-and-making-sense-of-everything.md) · Used by `DEV-IMG-08`, `DEV-SPM-05`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Version 20 of the Screaming Frog SEO Spider, released in May 2024, was the first that could connect the crawler to ChatGPT through custom JavaScript, which let SEOs rewrite image alt text at scale.
  <br><sub>`D2-C946` · Day 2, Lightning session F: Media (speaker not identified) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** In a community speaker's case, an LLM asked to write alt text for a product image of a veterinary anxiety medicine for cats described only what it could see, a cat and a veterinarian, and dropped the stress, anxiety and medical-treatment intent of the page.
  <br><sub>`D2-C947` · Day 2, Lightning session F: Media (speaker not identified) · Extends [D2-C462](../../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** After shipping LLM-rewritten image alt text on a client's site, a community speaker saw the site's image performance in Google Search Console drop (no figures were given).
  <br><sub>`D2-C948` · Day 2, Lightning session F: Media (speaker not identified)</sub>

- **[Stage]** To test LLM-generated alt text before a rollout, a community speaker recommended running the crawler's custom JavaScript in Screaming Frog's List mode on a few chosen URLs and reviewing the generated alt text, instead of crawling the whole site in Spider mode.
  <br><sub>`D2-C949` · Day 2, Lightning session F: Media (speaker not identified) · not in Google docs · Used by `DEV-IMG-02`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Because not every generated alt text can be checked by hand, a community speaker's safer script adds the page title to the LLM's image description, so the alt text carries the page's intent and not only what the image shows.
  <br><sub>`D2-C950` · Day 2, Lightning session F: Media (speaker not identified) · consistent with Google docs · [Google image SEO best practices](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-images) · Extends [D2-C537](../../40-sessions/day2/D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md) · Used by `DEV-IMG-02`</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker named the limits of the title-based alt-text script: it rewrites only the hero image, assumes the page title states the user's intent, had been tested in only one language or market, and runs on the free Gemini model.
  <br><sub>`D2-C951` · Day 2, Lightning session F: Media (speaker not identified)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A community speaker warned that articles still recommend rewriting alt text with AI, called AI a tool, and said that adopting such new AI implementations without applying existing SEO knowledge can damage ranking performance.
  <br><sub>`D2-C952` · Day 2, Lightning session F: Media (speaker not identified) · Extends [D2-C462](../../40-sessions/day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md)</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's Discover slide said that for eligible content image quality decides click-through: a small thumbnail lowers the click-through rate and a large, high-resolution image raises it.
  <br><sub>`D3-C221` · Day 3, Uncovering Trustworthy Experiences on Discover (Google) · consistent with Google docs · [Discover and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover) · Used by `DEV-IMG-07`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's Discover slide recommended large images at least 1,200 px wide, with more than 300,000 total pixels and a 16x9 aspect ratio, enabled by the max-image-preview:large setting.
  <br><sub>`D3-C224` · Day 3, Uncovering Trustworthy Experiences on Discover (Google) · confirmed by Google docs · [Discover and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover) · Extends [D2-C089](../../40-sessions/day2/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) · Repeats [D2-C936](../../40-sessions/day2/D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md) · Used by `DEV-IDX-04`, `DEV-IMG-07`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's Discover slide said to avoid generic images, such as a site logo, and text-heavy images.
  <br><sub>`D3-C225` · Day 3, Uncovering Trustworthy Experiences on Discover (Google) · confirmed by Google docs · [Discover and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover) · Used by `DEV-IMG-07`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's Discover slide said images are subject to the same policy requirements as the content and that misleading, exaggerated or outrageous images should be avoided.
  <br><sub>`D3-C226` · Day 3, Uncovering Trustworthy Experiences on Discover (Google) · consistent with Google docs · [Discover and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover), [Discover content policies](https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/9982767?hl=en) · Used by `DEV-IMG-07`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google said it shows images on the web results page, not only in image search, because from 2005-2006 it saw people appending words such as 'pictures' or 'images' to their queries, which led to the launch of universal search.
  <br><sub>`D3-C306` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs · Used by the glossary term *Universal search*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google handles an image used as a search query much like a text query interpreted as an embedding: the image is broken down into vectors (embeddings) that are then searched for in the index.
  <br><sub>`D3-C311` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs · Extends [D2-C740](../../40-sessions/day2/D2-S23-how-does-the-index-look-like.md) · Repeats [D1-C224](../../40-sessions/day1/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google can still detect intent for image queries, even though they are searched as embeddings, the speaker said.
  <br><sub>`D3-C312` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Image results shown among web results come from Google's image index and are roughly the same images that Google Images shows for the same query.
  <br><sub>`D3-C319` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs · Extends [D2-C525](../../40-sessions/day2/D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Product annotations on Google Images results also come from product structured data and do not need Google Merchant Center.
  <br><sub>`D3-C345` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [Introduction to Product structured data](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/product) · Used by `DEV-SHP-01`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google's Search Console talk presented multimodal search reporting as its fifth and newest launch, under a 'Hot from the oven' badge.
  > "5. Multimodal search reporting"
  <br><sub>`D3-C454` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · confirmed by Google docs · [Announcing web multimodal Search performance reporting in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/09/web-multimodal-in-sc)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Multimodal search reporting in Search Console launched about a week and a half before the 2 October 2026 talk.
  <br><sub>`D3-C455` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · consistent with Google docs · [Announcing web multimodal Search performance reporting in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/09/web-multimodal-in-sc)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google said searching with images is convenient for users and drives traffic to websites.
  <br><sub>`D3-C456` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · consistent with Google docs · [Announcing web multimodal Search performance reporting in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/09/web-multimodal-in-sc)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Multimodal searches reported in Search Console include searches with Google Lens, Circle to Search on Android, images uploaded to Google Search and Chrome's right-click search on an image.
  <br><sub>`D3-C458` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · confirmed by Google docs · [Announcing web multimodal Search performance reporting in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/09/web-multimodal-in-sc), [Performance report (Search results): Overview and basic setup](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7576553?hl=en) · Used by `DEV-MON-07`, the glossary term *Multimodal search type*</sub>

- **[Stage]** To see multimodal traffic in the Search Console Performance report, select the multimodal search type instead of the default text-based one.
  <br><sub>`D3-C459` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · consistent with Google docs · [Announcing web multimodal Search performance reporting in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/09/web-multimodal-in-sc), [Performance report (Search results): Overview and basic setup](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7576553?hl=en) · Used by `DEV-MON-07`, the glossary term *Multimodal search type*</sub>

- **[Stage]** In a live demo, Google Lens on an Android phone identified a photographed object and listed websites selling it, with deep links that allow buying it online.
  <br><sub>`D3-C460` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · consistent with Google docs · [Search with Google Lens in Chrome](https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/15086890?hl=en), [Search with an image on Google](https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/1325808?hl=en)</sub>

- **[Stage]** In a demo, asking Chrome about an image on a web page opened a side panel of visual matches, one of which was on Google's developers site and led on to more information about Search Console; Google described this as the full flow of the multimodal traffic now reported.
  <br><sub>`D3-C461` · Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It (Ariel Kroszynski) · consistent with Google docs · [Search with Google Lens in Chrome](https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/15086890?hl=en), [Announcing web multimodal Search performance reporting in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/09/web-multimodal-in-sc)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google indexes images in hours to two days on average, and the fastest it can reliably index an image is under 150 seconds.
  <br><sub>`D3-C648` · Day 3, How long does it take to..? (Gary Illyes) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google tries to index images from news sites much faster than usual, which lowers the average image indexing time (the reading 'news sites' is likely but not certain).
  <br><sub>`D3-C649` · Day 3, How long does it take to..? (Gary Illyes) · not in Google docs</sub>

## What Google's documentation says

- **[Docs]** Google's May 2025 Search announcement says more than 1.5 billion people use Google Lens to search what they see every month.
  > "Google Lens, which more than 1.5 billion people are using to search what they see every month"
  <br><sub>`D1-C191` · Google blog (20 May 2025) · annotates Day 1, What's new in the world of Search · is the documentation · [AI in Search: Going beyond information to intelligence](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/google-search-ai-mode-update/) · Used by the glossary term *Google Lens*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's robots meta tag specification says that with nosnippet a static image thumbnail, if available, may still be shown when that results in a better user experience.
  <br><sub>`D2-C071` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Controlling indexing · is the documentation · [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's documented ways to keep a site's images out of search results are a robots.txt disallow rule (for example for Googlebot-Image) or a noindex X-Robots-Tag HTTP header, with the Removals tool for emergencies.
  <br><sub>`D2-C529` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos · is the documentation · [Remove images hosted on your site from search results](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/prevent-images-on-your-page) · Used by `DEV-IDX-03`, `DEV-IMG-06`, the glossary term *X-Robots-Tag*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's image SEO guide calls alt text the most important attribute for providing more metadata about an image, and says Google uses it together with computer vision and the page content to understand the image.
  > "The most important attribute when it comes to providing more metadata for an image is the alt text"
  <br><sub>`D2-C534` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos · is the documentation · [Google image SEO best practices](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-images) · Used by `DEV-IMG-02`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's image SEO guide lists AVIF among the supported image formats (with BMP, GIF, JPEG, PNG, WebP and SVG), and Google announced in August 2024 that AVIF files need nothing special to be indexed.
  <br><sub>`D2-C543` · Google Search Central, Search Central blog (30 August 2024) · annotates Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos · is the documentation · [Google image SEO best practices](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-images), [Supporting AVIF in Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/08/happy-avifriday) · Used by `DEV-IMG-05`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's image metadata guide says Google Images supports the IPTC Digital Source Type values for algorithmically created images, such as trainedAlgorithmicMedia, and can show C2PA details in 'About this image', such as whether an image was created or edited with AI tools.
  <br><sub>`D2-C943` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos · is the documentation · [Image metadata in Google Images](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/image-license-metadata) · Used by `DEV-IMG-08`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's Discover documentation says to specify the large image with schema.org markup or the og:image meta tag, which can influence the thumbnail Discover chooses, and that a vertical image cropped to 16x9 must keep its important details.
  <br><sub>`D3-C227` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, Uncovering Trustworthy Experiences on Discover · is the documentation · [Discover and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover) · Used by `DEV-IMG-07`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's announcement of 24 September 2026 says multimodal search data appears both in the Performance report for Search results and in the generative AI performance report, can be exported, and began rolling out globally that day.
  <br><sub>`D3-C465` · Search Central blog (24 September 2026) · annotates Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It · is the documentation · [Announcing web multimodal Search performance reporting in Search Console](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2026/09/web-multimodal-in-sc) · Used by `DEV-MON-07`, the glossary term *Generative AI performance report*, the glossary term *Multimodal search type*</sub>

## Analysis

- **[Analysis]** Visual search predates transformers in Google's own history: its Search timeline dates Google Images to 2001 and Google Lens to 2017, the year Google Research published the Transformer, so read the stage remark as being about today's multimodal AI search.
  <br><sub>`D1-C200` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 1, What's new in the world of Search · [25 biggest moments in Search, from helpful images to AI](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/search/25-biggest-google-search-updates/), [Transformer: A Novel Neural Network Architecture for Language Understanding](https://research.google/blog/transformer-a-novel-neural-network-architecture-for-language-understanding/)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** With one in six AI Mode searches being multimodal, original images with descriptive file names, alt text and captions feed AI answers as well as image search.
  <br><sub>`D1-C117` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 1, session not recorded · Extended by [D2-C525](../../40-sessions/day2/D2-S13-using-images-to-your-advantage-and-engaging-search-users-with-videos.md)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Set max-snippet:-1 and max-image-preview:large on every indexable template unless licensing requires otherwise, and check that no CMS, plug-in or CDN setting adds lower snippet or image preview limits by default.
  <br><sub>`D2-C105` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Controlling indexing · Used by `DEV-IDX-04`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Hiding an image as a CSS background is a fragile way to keep it out of Google: it only stops extraction from that page, so the same image URL used in an img element elsewhere or listed in a sitemap can still be indexed; the documented robots.txt or noindex X-Robots-Tag methods are the reliable route.
  <br><sub>`D2-C530` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos · [Remove images hosted on your site from search results](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/prevent-images-on-your-page), [Google image SEO best practices](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-images) · Used by `DEV-IMG-06`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Images that should rank need an img element with a real src; hero or product images set as CSS backgrounds are invisible to Google Images and image features, so keep CSS backgrounds for decorative images you do not need indexed.
  <br><sub>`D2-C538` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos · Used by `DEV-IMG-01`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Give important images a caption or explanatory sentence next to them rather than relying on alt text alone, since Gary Illyes ranked src above alt and called the surrounding text critical for ranking the image.
  <br><sub>`D2-C539` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos · Used by `DEV-IMG-03`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** While the AVIF ingestion hiccup Gary Illyes mentioned lasts, serve AVIF only through source elements inside picture and keep a WebP or JPEG file in the img src, which is the URL Google extracts, even though Google's documentation lists AVIF as supported; then check in Google Images that key images appear.
  <br><sub>`D2-C545` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Using images to your advantage and Engaging Search users with videos · [Google image SEO best practices](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-images), [Supporting AVIF in Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/08/happy-avifriday) · Used by `DEV-IMG-05`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** For Discover, set max-image-preview:large on article templates, give every article a relevant image at least 1,200 px wide in og:image or schema.org markup that is neither the site logo nor text-heavy, and show clear bylines and dates.
  <br><sub>`D3-C230` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Uncovering Trustworthy Experiences on Discover · [Discover and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover), [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag) · Used by `DEV-IMG-07`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Google's Performance report help says the queries dimension is not available for the multimodal search type, because these searches mostly use images, so judge image-led traffic by page, country and device, and make product and article images distinctive enough for Lens to match.
  <br><sub>`D3-C462` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 3, Inside Search Console: What’s New & How to Use It · Used by `DEV-MON-07`</sub>

## Built on these claims

The items of the developer and content kits that rest on this topic's claims.

- Requirement `DEV-IDX-03`: Send robots rules for PDFs, images and other non-HTML files in the X-Robots-Tag header
- Requirement `DEV-IDX-04`: Allow full snippets and large previews with max-snippet:-1 and max-image-preview:large
- Requirement `DEV-IDX-09`: Leave notranslate and noimageindex out of templates unless translation or image indexing must be prevented
- Requirement `DEV-IMG-01`: Put every image that should be found in an `<img>` element with a src attribute
- Requirement `DEV-IMG-02`: Describe every meaningful image in its alt attribute
- Requirement `DEV-IMG-03`: Place images next to text that explains them
- Requirement `DEV-IMG-04`: List important images in an image sitemap
- Requirement `DEV-IMG-05`: Serve modern, compact image formats with a widely supported file in the img src
- Requirement `DEV-IMG-06`: Keep images out of Search with robots.txt or X-Robots-Tag, not with CSS tricks
- Requirement `DEV-IMG-07`: Give every article a large, relevant lead image and declare it in og:image or markup
- Requirement `DEV-IMG-08`: Keep the IPTC and C2PA metadata that marks AI-generated images
- Requirement `DEV-MON-07`: Track AI feature visibility in the Generative AI performance report
- Requirement `DEV-SHP-01`: Use Product markup for rich results and a Merchant Center feed for the Shopping tab, with identical values
- Requirement `DEV-SPM-05`: Publish AI-generated text, images and markup only after human review, and show only real authors
- Requirement `DEV-VID-06`: Serve videos fast in a common container with standard codecs, and never block the files
- Glossary term *Generative AI performance report*
- Glossary term *Google Lens*
- Glossary term *Googlebot-Image and Googlebot-Video*
- Glossary term *max-image-preview*
- Glossary term *Multimodal search type*
- Glossary term *noimageindex*
- Glossary term *Universal search*
- Glossary term *X-Robots-Tag*
